bug_semantics: CWE-426/CWE-427 untrusted search path: two NLTK Graphviz helpers executed the `dot` program by bare name (`subprocess.Popen`/`subprocess.run` argv starting with `"dot"`), so the OS resolved the binary via PATH and, on Windows, the current working directory. An attacker who can plant a file named `dot` in CWD or a relative/writable PATH entry gets that binary executed instead of Graphviz (arbitrary code execution). At <=3.10.2, `nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img` called `find_binary("dot")` but discarded the returned absolute path and still ran `["dot", ...]`; `nltk.translate.api.AlignedSent._repr_svg_` ran the bare name with no validation. `DependencyGraph._repr_svg_` had been refactored to call `dot2img`, so it inherited the same sink. The 3.10.3 fix runs the absolute path `find_binary` already returns (it refuses a CWD-relative match for a bare tool name).
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism — spawning Graphviz `dot` by bare name — was first written in nltk/parse/dependencygraph.py `DependencyGraph._repr_svg_` by human commit b271b4def63fda07df8ecfe888cd4c663ede2b05 (2015-02-19, PR #891). Those Popen(['dot', ...]) lines are absent in the immediate parent. A later independent copy landed in AlignedSent._repr_svg_ (d72c69d5, 2015-05-08, then a package move to nltk/translate/api.py). In 2021 squash #2740 (8f913258) the DependencyGraph call was extracted into new helper `dot2img` and rewritten as subprocess.run(["dot", ...]); in 2022 #3048 (9851f746) `find_binary("dot")` was added but its return value was unused, which is the discarded-validation shape named in the advisory. Extraction, move, Black quote-style, and the unused find_binary check are not BICs.
